items.title: Batch removal of all unused OpenPGP keys

labels.name: RFE
labels.description: Request For Enhancement (as opposed to a bug)

labels.name: Triaged
labels.description: Someone on the DNF 5 team has read the issue and determined the next steps to take

items.body:
There's a cool feature that detects expired keys. It seems that any time I run `dnf update`, expired keys are identified and removed:

```
The following OpenPGP key (0x24C1DC34) is about to be removed:
 Reason     : Expired on 2025-09-24 14:27:40
 UserID     : "rhcopr-project_toolset (None) <rhcopr-project#toolset@copr.fedorahosted.org>"
 Fingerprint: E633590202A9355BE369257DC8E87D4D24C1DC34

As a result, installing packages signed with this key will fail.
It is recommended to remove the expired key to allow importing
an updated key. This might leave already installed packages unverifiable.

The system will now proceed with removing the key.
Is this ok [y/N]: y
Key 0x24C1DC34 was successfully removed.
```

This situation has become pretty annoying because keys have accumulated on my box over the years.

It would be great to have a tool—something like `dnf eliminate-unused-keys`—that could identify the set of GPG keys that aren't currently used (no enabled repository is refering to that key?  no installed RPM is signed by that key?) and removed since they are no longer needed for trust.

items.title: RFE: Notify User About Unused Dependencies After Package Operations

labels.name: RFE
labels.description: Request For Enhancement (as opposed to a bug)

labels.name: Triaged
labels.description: Someone on the DNF 5 team has read the issue and determined the next steps to take

items.body:
It appears that when a package is replaced (e.g., upgraded, downgraded, or reinstalled) and the new package no longer requires some of the original dependencies, those no longer-needed dependencies remain on the system. These unused dependencies can be removed by subsequently running `dnf autoremove`.

It would be beneficial to notify the user if new unused dependencies are created as a result of a package operation.

Proposed Functionality:
After a dnf operation that involves package replacement, consider displaying a message to the user such as:
- Notification of newly unused dependencies: "Operation caused 123 new unused dependencies to be present on your system."
- Total unused dependencies and hint: "There are now a total of 456 unused dependencies on your system. You can remove them by running `dnf autoremove`."

- Optional: List newly unused dependencies.

This feature would help users keep their systems cleaner and more efficient by making them aware of orphaned dependencies and providing a clear path to their removal.

Maybe it was just like that with `dnf` but I'm not sure.

items.title: Protected packages break autoremoval of unsed dependencies

labels.name: downstream
labels.description: Also reported in Jira or Bugzilla

items.body:
It seems that protected packages break automatic removal of unused dependencies:

~~~~
# dnf5 install kiwi-systemdeps-bootloaders
[...]
# dnf5 remove kiwi-systemdeps-bootloaders
Failed to resolve the transaction:
Problem: The operation would result in removing the following protected packages: grub2-efi-ia32, grub2-efi-x64
~~~~

Affected packages:

dnf5-5.2.5.0-20240805005756.19.g04d9908f.fc41.x86_64
libsolv-0.7.30-20240805005745.0.g27aa6a72.fc41.x86_64

Observed with Fedora 41 buildroot repository.
